The *Dīpikaṅgapañha* ("The Panther", Mil 7.2.5) is a section within the *Milindapañha* [SuttaCentral]. Like other discourses in this portion of the collection, it expounds spiritual practice and monastic qualities through the analogy of an animal—here drawing upon the characteristics (*aṅga*) of a panther (*dīpi*) [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral records three modern translations across three languages [SuttaCentral].

The text also shares significant recurring phrasing with neighboring simile discourses in the seventh book of the *Milindapañha*, such as the *Pabbataṅgapañha* (Mil 7.4.5), *Ākāsaṅgapañha* (Mil 7.4.6), and *Kukkuṭaṅgapañha* (Mil 7.2.2), as well as exegetical and doctrinal treatises including the *Sāriputtasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 16), *Khaggavisāṇasuttaniddesa* (Cnd 23), and the *Jhānavibhaṅga* (Vb 12) [DharmaNexus].
